# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 2

**1** When she had finished speaking, she said, "Would you like me to read to you?" "Yes, my lady," I said. "Then listen," she replied. She opened the small book and read to me — not from the beginning, but from somewhere in the middle, as follows: **2** "Behold, O God of Powers, who by your invisible and great might, and by your abundant wisdom, created the world — who by your glorious design clothed your creation with loveliness, and by your powerful word set the heavens in place and founded the earth upon the waters, and by your own wisdom and providence formed your holy church, which you also blessed — **3** behold, he is removing the heavens and the mountains and the hills and the seas, and all things will be made level for his chosen ones, so that he may fulfill to them the promise he made with great glory and joy, if they keep the commandments of God which they received in great faith." **4** When she had finished reading I arose and said, "Lady, what does it mean that the heavens and the mountains and the hills and the seas will be removed?" She replied, "All these things, when they are removed, must serve the chosen of God. For all these mountains and hills and seas and heavens stand as enemies of the elect and must be removed. Then those who are faithful and single-hearted will enjoy good things, but the wicked will not enter in." **5** She said to me, "I want you to understand that it is I alone who am all these things: patience and love and truth, and the foundation and building-up and protective wall and tower and power of the saints." I said, "Lady, explain this to me." She said, "Do you not see before you the great tower being built upon the waters, with bright squared stones?"

---

### Council Notes

The Church's self-identification (v. 5) is the theological climax of Vision 2: she is simultaneously patient, loving, truthful, and all the architectural metaphors of the tower vision (foundation, wall, tower). This is a profoundly corporate ecclesiology.

The tower upon the water (v. 5) previews the extended allegory of Vision 3, which is the longest section of the Visions. Building on water may allude to the baptismal foundation of the Church.

"Single-hearted" (haplous) is the positive counterpart to "double-minded" (dipsychos). The two poles — wholehearted faith vs. vacillating doubt — are the Shepherd's key moral categories.
